conbody.p: When you sign in or open the app, OpenV takes you to the Home page of the project you opened last (or of the workspace's first project, the first time). A workspace with no projects yet starts here instead, on the Projects page, so you can create one. To come back to the list, choose Projects in the menu or All projects on Home.

The Projects page lists the active workspace's projects as rows. Each row shows the project's name and how many artifacts it holds, a one-line description, and two bars: the share of its requirements that are traced (a test case verifies them) and the share verified. A project with no requirements yet says so instead. The project you opened last is marked with a blue edge, and the head of the page counts the workspace's projects. Each row carries its action buttons:

strow.stentry: Save as template — snapshot this project as a reusable template
Edit project — rename it or change the description
Download — opens the download wizard (format, sections, attachments)
Delete project — removes the project and all its artifacts

conbody.p: Click anywhere else on the row to open the project.
